issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add support for rendering [mermaid charts](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid) in Streamlit.

### Why?

Mermaid is a popular, text-based diagramming tool integrated into tools like Github & Notion. It provides a variety of diagrams that could also be useful for Streamlit apps. 

### How?

There are a couple of options for how this could be implemented:
1. Add support for mermaid charts as part of the markdown rendering (e.g. via code blocks)
2. Provide a `st.mermaid_chart` command that allows rendering a mermaid string.
3. Do 1 + 2.

### Additional Context

- Remark plugin for renderin mermaid charts:
    - https://github.com/remcohaszing/remark-mermaidjs
    - https://github.com/temando/remark-mermaid
    - https://github.com/remcohaszing/rehype-mermaid
- [Mermaid Playground](https://mermaid-js.github.io/mermaid-live-editor/edit)
- [mkdocs support via markdown code blocks](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/reference/diagrams/#using-state-diagrams)
- [Github support via markdown code blocks](https://github.blog/developer-skills/github/include-diagrams-markdown-files-mermaid/)
- Related Streamlit forum posts: [1](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/st-markdown-does-not-render-mermaid-graphs/25576) & [2](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/streamlit-markdown-a-streaming-markdown-component-with-latex-mermaid-table-code-support/72187)

No code is changed — this consolidated review focuses on the quality, completeness, and consistency of the spec itself. All three reviewers agreed this is a well-scoped, low-risk, spec-only PR and converged on **APPROVED** with non-blocking refinements. ## Code Quality The spec is well-structured and closely follows `specs/YYYY-MM-DD-template/product-spec.md`: frontmatter, problem/pain-points/use-cases framing, proposed API with progressive examples, behavior, security, accessibility, tradeoffs, backwards-compatibility, out-of-scope, alternatives considered, and the checklist. Reviewers agreed the document is comprehensive and ready for implementation planning. A few cross-cutting concerns worth discussing at the spec level (specific line-level findings are flagged as inline comments): - **Primary motivator ↔ scope mismatch.** The Problem section explicitly cites AI chat applications (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) as a reason Mermaid has become a de-facto standard, but the Proposal restricts rendering to `st.markdown` and explicitly excludes `st.chat_message` along with tooltips, help text, table cells, and widget labels. That is a defensible scoping choice, but the spec should briefly justify it given how prominently AI chat is used to motivate the feature — otherwise reviewers will wonder why the most obvious use case is out of scope at launch. - **Consistency with other chart commands.** `st.graphviz_chart`, `st.plotly_chart`, `st.altair_chart`, etc. all expose `width`/`height` (and historically `use_container_width`). The "Intentional Simplicity" section argues for `body`-only, which fits API principle #4 (Start Minimal) but tensions with #5 (Consistency Over Novelty) and #10 (Same Name, Same Behavior). Worth promoting this decision into "Alternatives Considered" with an explicit option comparison so the tradeoff is visible to reviewers rather than tucked into an implementation note. - **Implementation-vs-product framing.** The "Implementation Note" stating that `st.mermaid_chart` internally calls `st.markdown` is a tech-spec concern; locking it into the product spec risks making the doc stale if a dedicated element is later chosen for better toolbar/loading UX. ## Test Coverage N/A — spec-only change. The PR description correctly states "Spec-only change, no code modifications." The implementation PR will need to ship targeted frontend unit and e2e coverage for: mixed markdown content (mermaid fence alongside headings/paragraphs), theme switching (dark/light), toolbar actions (fullscreen, PNG download, copy source), error rendering for invalid Mermaid syntax, and the documented backwards-compatibility behavior of the `mermaid` fence in `st.markdown`. ## Backwards Compatibility Reviewers agreed the spec correctly flags the behavior change ("⚠️") and dedicates a full "Backwards Compatibility" section to it: `st.markdown("```mermaid\n...```")` will switch from rendering as a plain code block to rendering as a diagram. The rationale (parity with GitHub/GitLab/Notion/Obsidian) and the proposed escape hatch (`st.code(mermaid_source, language="mermaid")`) are reasonable and called out prominently in the checklist too. Two follow-ups worth confirming before implementation lands: 1. The "syntax highlighting" claim for the `language="mermaid"` escape hatch only holds if Prism's mermaid grammar is actually registered in `StreamlitSyntaxHighlighter` — see inline comment. 2. This kind of breaking change benefits from an explicit announcement in release notes, which the docs row of the checklist should probably capture. ## Security & Risk No security-sensitive code paths are changed in this PR — the only diff is a new markdown file under `specs/`. The spec's security discussion is appropriately concrete: `securityLevel: "strict"` (disables HTML labels, strips `foreignObject`) and SVG rendered via blob URL inside `` (prevents inline script execution). Points worth clarifying in the follow-up tech spec: - CSP: confirm the served default CSP allows `img-src blob:` and that strict-CSP deployments and embedded iframes / SiS still work. If the implementation ever falls back to inline SVG in any code path, the XSS surface and CSP story change meaningfully. - Mermaid.js becomes part of the trusted client runtime; ongoing CVE / supply-chain monitoring (pinning strategy, dependency review cadence) is worth a one-liner in Tradeoffs. No other security-sensitive areas (auth, sessions, uploads, cookies, XSRF, OAuth, headers) are touched by this PR. ## External test recommendation - **Recommend external_test:** No - **Triggered categories:** None - **Evidence:** The only change is a new markdown file under `specs/`. No routing, auth, session/WebSocket, embed/iframe, storage, CSP/CORS, asset-serving, SiS, or Python runtime code is modified by this PR. Confirmed via the diff: a single `.md` file added. - **Suggested external_test focus areas (for the implementation PR, not this one):** embedded/iframe rendering, CSP compatibility (blob URLs), cross-origin behavior of the SVG ``, and SiS / Community Cloud asset loading for the lazy-loaded mermaid.js chunk. - **Confidence:** High. Assumption: no accompanying code changes are intended in this branch; the planned feature may warrant external coverage once implementation details land. All three reviewers independently reached the same "No / None / High confidence" recommendation. ## Accessibility The Accessibility section is present and mentions semantic alt text, `aria-busy="true"`, descriptive `aria-label`, `role="alert"` for errors, and proper labeling for the fullscreen button. Directionally good, and largely not verifiable until the implementation PR. The most important gap to address before implementation: rendering the SVG inside an `` via blob URL means assistive tech cannot read the SVG's inner ``/`<desc>` nodes or per-node labels, so a generic alt such as "Mermaid flowchart" only signals "there is a diagram here", not its contents. Consider surfacing Mermaid's `accTitle:` / `accDescr:` directives as the `alt` text, allowing users to override it, or using inline SVG with sanitization. At minimum, document the limitation explicitly. (Tracked as a high-severity inline comment.) ## Recommendations 1. Add a brief explanation for why `st.chat_message` and other markdown-bearing surfaces are excluded at launch, given AI chat is cited as a primary motivator. 2. Promote the `body`-only design decision into "Alternatives Considered" with an explicit option comparison against `width`/`height`/`use_container_width` (matching `st.graphviz_chart` / `st.plotly_chart`), and reference API principles #4/#5/#10. 3. Add an accessibility plan for diagram *content* (leveraging Mermaid `accTitle:` / `accDescr:` or a user-specified description), not just the container chrome. 5. Clarify whether Mermaid theming tracks user-configured `[theme]` overrides in `config.toml` or is pinned to the built-in Streamlit palette. 9. Author a companion tech spec before implementation begins to lock down markdown-renderer scoping, lazy-loading/security model, telemetry mechanism, and cross-surface behavior. ## Verdict **APPROVED**: Spec-only change that follows the template, is well-written, and surfaces the right tradeoffs; all three reviewers approved and the remaining items are non-blocking refinements best addressed via inline comments before implementation begins. --- *This is an automated AI review consolidated by `claude-opus-4-7-thinking-xhigh` from individual reviews by `gpt-5.4-xhigh`, `gemini-3.1-pro`, and `claude-opus-4-7-thinking-xhigh`.
